page.layout: One printed page: a woodcut diagram of a circle with twelve numbered sectors at top; below it a centred heading and the running text in full width; a catchword-like signature line at the foot right. Margins: handwritten annotations (not printed) around the diagram, to be ignored.

main_text.head: DE HORIZONTE.
main_text.p: FINITOREM latini uocant & circulum hemisphærij, quem οριζοντα graeci, ἀπὸ τοῦ ὁρίζειν, quod uisum finit ac terminat.

Est autem Horizon circulus maior, immotus, nō unus idemq; ubiuis, sed cuilibet locus proprius, à puncto uerticali, circūquaq; æquabiliter distans & totam mundi sphæram, dirimens in hemisphæria æqualia, quorum alterum eminet & conspicitur supra nos, alterum sub terra occultatur.

page.notes: Diagram of a circle divided into twelve sectors with numbers 1–12, labels Oriens, Occidens, Meridies (MER.), Septentrio (SEP.), Media nox/Mediæ noctis and Horizon; handwritten annotations in the margins are not transcribed. The Greek in the first paragraph is a reconstruction from a small, blurred print: Greek words "ὁρίζοντα" and "ἀπὸ τοῦ ὁρίζοντος" are doubtful. Catchword "Distin" is partly cut off at the margin.
